title: Nitzavim: choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19)
hook: "I have set before thee life and death... therefore choose life"

segments.voice: Yesterday, the word that's very near, in your mouth and in your heart. Your line was very near. Today, the last lines of Nitzavim, and a choice.

At Jewish celebrations, sooner or later someone lifts a glass and says l'chaim. To life. Over wine at a wedding, over whiskey at a bris, over a paper cup at a retirement party. It's so ordinary that it's easy to miss what the toast picks: not luck, not health, not money. Life. Today's verse puts that same word, chayim, life, at the center of the choice Moses sets before the people.
screen: `A GLASS LIFTED.` → `L'CHAIM: TO LIFE.` → `THE SAME WORD IN THE TORAH.`

segments.voice: Moses is near the end of his speech. He calls heaven and earth to witness and says: "I have set before thee life and death, the blessing and the curse; therefore choose life, that thou mayest live, thou and thy seed." Notice the odd extra step. If someone offered you life or death, you wouldn't need advice about which to pick. So why say it? Rashi imagines a father with his son. He stands the boy in front of the best plot of his land and says: choose this one for yourself. The advice isn't there because the answer is hard to see. It's love, pointing. Another reading hears the verse as a statement that the choice is real. Maimonides, the philosopher and legal scholar, drew on this chapter in his teaching on free will. A person isn't fated to be good or bad. Each person can choose. And the verses right after say what life means here: to love God, to listen, to hold fast. Life, in this verse, is more than breathing. It's a way of living that leads to more life. Then the last words: thou and thy seed. Your choice reaches your children. Choosing life is rarely one big moment. It's made of small ones: a glass lifted, a meal shared, a hard thing faced instead of avoided, a day lived toward something good.
screen: `LIFE AND DEATH, SET BEFORE YOU.` · `RASHI: A FATHER POINTING.` · `MAIMONIDES: THE CHOICE IS REAL.` · `THOUSANDS OF SMALL CHOICES.` · then, large: `CHOOSE LIFE.`

segments.voice: Think about the rest of today and find one fork in it, maybe a small one: eat something real or skip it, go outside or stay in, call someone or keep scrolling, rest or push through when you shouldn't. Name it, and picture taking the side that gives a little more life, to you or to someone else.
Nitzavim. Standing. And the choice set before everyone standing there: life.
Your line: choose life. And if you lift a glass tonight, you'll know the toast. Day five hundred twenty-one, done.

howItsDone: 'Choose life' is often quoted in Jewish teaching on ethics and free will, and the toast l'chaim, 'to life', is a familiar sound at Jewish celebrations.

options: Rashi hears love pointing, like a father showing his son the best field.
Moses meant it as a trick question, to test whether they were listening.
It's about danger: choosing life means never taking any risk at all.
